articles.title: Monitor your competitors' Chrome extension reviews with a scheduled scraper
articles.excerpt: If you build a Chrome extension, your competitors' 1-star reviews tell you what their users want and aren't getting. The Chrome Web Store has no export or alerts for other people's extensions, so the…
articles.body: If you build a Chrome extension, your competitors' 1-star reviews tell you what their users want and aren't getting. The Chrome Web Store has no export or alerts for other people's extensions, so the usual option is checking by hand. Here's a small setup: a scheduled scraper collects the latest reviews of a handful of competing extensions every day, and a short Python script flags the new low-rated ones. We'll use the App Store, Google Play & Chrome Web Store Reviews Scraper on Apify for collection and Apify's built-in Schedules for timing. The idea Pick 3–10 competing extensions. Run the scraper on a schedule (say, daily) with a modest maxReviewsPerApp .

articles.title: I built a support copilot for one-person shops that runs Gemma 4 on a laptop
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 2: Side Hustle Picture a one-person online shop selling handmade ceramics. The owner makes the mugs, photographs them, packs th…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 2: Side Hustle What I Built Picture a one-person online shop selling handmade ceramics. The owner makes the mugs, photographs them, packs them... and every evening answers the same emails: "my mug arrived cracked", "my parcel is late", "can I get a refund?". She already knows the answers. She just has to write them again, consistently, every single time. Little Kiln Support Copilot drafts those replies for her. You paste a customer message; it finds how you solved similar cases before and writes a draft that follows your own policies. You review it and send it. Who would pay: solo makers and small shops on Etsy, Shopify or their own site, for whom support eats hours but a full helpdesk subscription is overkill.

articles.title: What Ten Site Icon Generator Results Actually Produced From One PNG
articles.excerpt: A site icon generator is useful only when its downloaded files match the formats and sizes your site needs. In a one-image test across ten result pages, three produced the complete package I checked f…
articles.body: A site icon generator is useful only when its downloaded files match the formats and sizes your site needs. In a one-image test across ten result pages, three produced the complete package I checked for: an ICO file, an Apple touch PNG, and a web app manifest. Several other flows did not produce an inspectable result, and one download labeled as an ICO was actually a JPEG. How the test was run I used one transparent 512 × 512 PNG throughout the test. Its top-left pixel had alpha 0 and its center pixel had alpha 255. I followed each page’s default, no-sign-in workflow and inspected downloaded files locally when a download was available. The test ran on Windows 11 Pro with Chrome 155.0.8059.84 on October 18, 2026.

articles.title: The handover package: 10 things a client should hold when your project ends
articles.excerpt: "It works on the demo server" is not the same as "the client can keep running it without you." Most handover pain we've seen doesn't come from bad code. It comes from things that were never written do…
articles.body: "It works on the demo server" is not the same as "the client can keep running it without you." Most handover pain we've seen doesn't come from bad code. It comes from things that were never written down or never moved out of the developer's accounts. Here is the 10-item package we put together before the last invoice, with one line on why each matters and one way to verify it. The 10 items 1. Repository in the client's account Why: if the code lives only in your personal GitHub, the product becomes unfixable the day you're unreachable. Check: the client clones from their org and sees the full commit history, not a squashed zip. 2. Domain, cloud, app store and payment accounts in the client's name Why: only the account owner can renew, cancel or transfer.

articles.title: Day 03/90: Hybrid Search in RAG: Can Combining BM25 and Vector Search Find Better Evidence?
articles.excerpt: Your RAG app retrieves five chunks. They look relevant, but none actually answers the question. The LLM responds confidently anyway. The result? A fluent answer built on the wrong evidence. Before cha…
articles.body: Your RAG app retrieves five chunks. They look relevant, but none actually answers the question. The LLM responds confidently anyway. The result? A fluent answer built on the wrong evidence. Before changing the prompt or switching models, ask: Did the retriever find the evidence needed to answer? That’s the question I’ll explore by comparing BM25, vector search, and hybrid retrieval with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF). Where Vector Search Helps—and Where It Can Miss Vector search uses embeddings to find passages with similar meaning, even when the wording differs. Question: “How do I reset my password?” Document: “Recover account access by updating your credentials.” Semantic similarity can help connect these passages. But consider: How do I fix error AUTH_403 ?

articles.title: The Bell of Greystone
articles.excerpt: Role-Playing Games I must confess, when I was young, I got completely hooked on role-playing games. But I mean the classic tabletop RPGs, sitting around a table with friends and a Dungeon Master. Some…
articles.body: Role-Playing Games I must confess, when I was young, I got completely hooked on role-playing games. But I mean the classic tabletop RPGs, sitting around a table with friends and a Dungeon Master. Something that no computer RPG has ever managed to recreate. No matter how beautifully crafted the world or how exciting the story, something essential was always missing: the freedom of playing a character you truly become, fighting alongside your friends, and knowing that almost anything is possible. Not just endless hacking, slashing, and mountains of magic spells. I gained experience not only as a player but also as a Dungeon Master, creating adventures and building worlds. Skills that turned out to be surprisingly useful many times later in my life, and still are.

articles.excerpt: Japan's mission to Mars' moons could answer a decades old question dividing the origins of Phobos and Deimos between two conflicting theories, and make history as the first spacecraft to return to Ear…
articles.body: Japan's mission to Mars is one of the most ambitious in spaceflight history. It aims to become the first spacecraft to return to Earth from Mars orbit, carrying with it the first-ever samples from the Red Planet system. The mission, known as Martian Moons eXploration (MMX), is a first-of-its-kind endeavor to study the origin of Mars' moons Phobos and Deimos. The robust undertaking includes a landing on Phobos to collect the samples — which will likely be the first from the Mars system to return to Earth — and a search for evidence that could shed light on events during the formation of the solar system billions of years ago. articles.title: Computer scientist Margaret Hamilton was a problem-solver for the ages (op-ed)
articles.excerpt: The world will miss Margaret Hamilton, the pioneering programmer who helped NASA land Apollo astronauts on the moon. But we will always have her example to inspire us.
articles.body: Dean Robbins is a journalist and children's author. He contributed this article to Space.com's Expert Voices: Op-Ed & Insights . The pioneering computer scientist Margaret Hamilton , who died on Sept. 30 at age 90, played a key role in putting astronauts on the moon. She was a problem-solver extraordinaire, and it all started in early childhood. Considering the name "daddy longlegs" unfair to female arachnids, young Margaret decided to call half of them "mommy longlegs." Wondering why the neighborhood baseball players were all boys, she determined to join the team herself. As she grew up in the 1940s and '50s, Margaret noticed a similar problem with various professions. Why were doctors, judges and scientists almost always men?

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 18, 1963: France's Félicette Becomes the 1st Cat in Space! >^..^<
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 18, 1963, a cat went to space! Félicette was a French "catstronaut" who became the first and only feline to fly to space. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 18, 1963, a cat went to space! Félicette was a French "catstronaut" who became the first and only feline to fly to space. While the U.S. and Soviet Union were busy launching primates, dogs and humans, the French decided to join the space race by launching a cat. Félicette, a stray tuxedo cat from the streets of Paris, was a substitute for another cat named Felix, who somehow escaped on launch day. So Félicette went where no cat had ever gone before. She boarded a French Véronique AG1 rocket and soared 130 miles above the Earth before safely parachuting back down. Luckily Félicette made it home alive and well, unlike many of the other animal astronauts that flew during the space race. Félicette, the first cat to fly into space in October 1963, is seen her carrier pre-flight.

articles.title: Astronomers want your help finding 'missing' black holes in the Milky Way
articles.excerpt: A citizen science project is seeking volunteers to comb through NASA telescope data for telltale signs of the galaxy's hidden black holes.
articles.body: Astronomers estimate that our home galaxy, the Milky Way, has churned out more than 10 million black holes over its 13-billion-year history. Yet so far, they have found only 70. Now, a group of astronomers in the U.K. is trying to close that vast gap by enlisting the public. Their project, called Black Hole Hunters , is looking for volunteers with a computer and a few spare minutes to sift through troves of data gathered by a NASA space telescope. By flagging recognizable patterns that could point to a "missing" black hole , volunteers can help fast-track a search that would otherwise take years, the team says.

Sonified: Eagle Nebula Pillars Explanation: Yes, but have you ever experienced the Eagle Nebula with your ears ? The famous nebula M16 is best known for the feast it gives your eyes, highlighting bright young stars forming deep inside dark towering structures . These light-years long columns of cold gas and dust are some 6,500 light-years distant toward the constellation of the Serpent ( Serpens ).

articles.title: OpenAI models hacked a crypto wallet and breached more websites
articles.excerpt: The actions could have resulted in criminal charges had humans been behind the keyboard.
articles.body: OpenAI said internal models hacked two more websites, bypassed company-imposed browsing restrictions, and used exposed credentials to draw cryptocurrency from a wallet it couldn’t otherwise access, in the latest installment of disclosures of its agents performing unethical and likely illegal acts. The company on Thursday issued reports of four new incidents, all of which occurred in June. They come after the company revealed in July that internal test agents exploited a zero-day vulnerability in a tool designed to restrict their access to the Internet. They then broke into the network of AI tool provider Hugging Face. The agents took that illegal action to steal answers to a hacking test that weren’t available when completing the tasks on their own.
